questions.question: Why is the site planned first in Plan mode?

options.text: A plan is easy to change before a single file has been made
options.explanation: Correct. Changing the plan takes one message, changing a finished site takes more work.

options.text: Otherwise Claude refuses to make the site
options.explanation: Claude would make the site even without a plan. Planning is worth it because the result then matches your wishes better.

options.text: In Plan mode, Claude writes code faster
options.explanation: In Plan mode, Claude doesn’t write any code at all. It only plans.

questions.question: What does the limits part of the example prompt do?

options.text: It tells Claude what it may use and what the site must have
options.explanation: Exactly. Limits keep Claude from making the site too complicated.

options.text: It limits how long Claude’s answer may be
options.explanation: The limits are about how the site is made, not about the length of the answer.
Claude follows the limits. They are the third part of a good prompt: what, why and within which limits.
